signals.title: Fit inconsistency is the top Gen Z frustration
signals.statement: Fit inconsistency is the most cited top frustration among Gen Z survey respondents, ahead of price, and sizing and fit questions are a large share of support contacts from customers under 28. The signal is consistent across the survey, support and the focus group.

evidence.quote: Fit inconsistency is the single most cited pain point, named by 27% of Gen Z survey respondents as their top frustration.
Sizing and fit questions accounted for 31% of all Q3 support contacts from customers under 28.
Seven of the ten participants said they had abandoned a cart because the size chart did not match the brand they already owned.

metrics.label: Fit is the top frustration, Gen Z
Fit is the top frustration, aged 28+

caveats: Focus group findings come from ten participants.

signals.title: Speed expectations are not being met on social
signals.statement: Median first response time on social channels is more than double the service target, while fast delivery is rated essential by many Gen Z shoppers. Delivery speed is rarely the single top frustration, so it may act as a hygiene factor rather than a differentiator.

evidence.quote: Median first response time on social channels slipped to 9.5 hours in Q3 against a service target of 4 hours.
Delivery within three days was rated essential by 48% of Gen Z respondents, up sharply among those buying through social platforms.

metrics.label: Gen Z respondents naming delivery speed as top frustration

caveats: Delivery speed is a hygiene factor rather than the top frustration.

signals.title: Discovery and purchase are moving to social
signals.statement: Social Shop is the fastest-growing channel, and Gen Z respondents say they trust peer reviews and creator try-on videos more than brand advertising.

evidence.quote: Social Shop sales grew 142% quarter over quarter, the fastest of any channel.
57% of Gen Z respondents said they trust peer reviews and creator try on videos more than brand advertising.

metrics.label: Social Shop net sales growth, Q1 to Q2 2026

caveats: Social Shop is still small in absolute terms.

signals.title: Stated premium tolerance tops out around 15%
signals.statement: A meaningful minority of Gen Z respondents say they would pay a 15% premium for personalized fit, but acceptance falls steeply at 25%, and Gen Z rates itself more price sensitive than older customers.

evidence.quote: 38% of Gen Z respondents said they would pay a 15% premium for footwear personalized to their fit.
Stated willingness to pay drops steeply above a 15% premium, with only 12% of Gen Z respondents accepting a 25% premium.
Price sensitivity averages 3.9 on a five point scale, against 3.2 for older customers.
When offered a 15% premium tier for personalized fit, only 9% of pilot shoppers selected it; most chose the free monogram option.
evidence.note: In the pilot, far fewer shoppers chose the paid tier than the survey suggests.

caveats: Willingness to pay is stated, not observed.

signals.title: Rivals are investing in fit technology and customization
signals.statement: A made-to-order competitor is growing quickly and the premium incumbent runs in-store gait scanning, while Northstar's aided awareness among Gen Z trails that incumbent.

evidence.quote: Kinetic Lab reported net revenue of $148 million for fiscal 2025, an increase of 64% on the prior year.
Our Fit Lab gait scanning is live in 120 flagship and partner stores and has completed more than 900,000 scans.
Aided brand awareness of Northstar among Gen Z consumers stands at 46%, well behind the 71% recorded for Vantage Athletic.

caveats: Competitor figures are company-reported; Kinetic Lab's 6% return rate is the company's own claim, and analyst checks put it near 15%.

signals.title: Gen Z NPS is about half that of older customers
signals.statement: Gen Z NPS fell between the first and second quarters and sits well below the NPS of customers aged 28 and older.

evidence.quote: Gen Z NPS fell to 22 in Q2 from 28 in Q1.
Of the 400 Gen Z respondents, 160 were promoters, 168 passives and 72 detractors, producing an NPS of 22.
The 200 older respondents produced 116 promoters, 66 passives and 18 detractors, an NPS of 49.

opportunities.title: Cross-category Fit Promise
opportunities.status_rationale: Fit friction is the most consistent signal across survey, support, focus group and returns data; the open question is cost, not demand.
opportunities.thesis: A fit guarantee may address the top Gen Z frustration and supports the stated positioning as the dependable fit brand.

evidence.quote: We recommend launching a cross category Fit Promise, a free exchange guarantee covering every apparel and footwear size, in Q1 FY27.
Participants ranked fit guarantee, faster delivery and honest materials information ahead of personalization when asked to spend a hypothetical 100 points.
I wear a medium in your joggers but a large in your hoodies, and my shoe size changes between your running and court lines.
Northstar intends to position itself as the dependable fit brand for active Gen Z consumers rather than competing on elite performance claims.
reason: Fit - runs small; total_sku_returns: 1421; returns_count: 583; share_of_sku_returns_pct: 41
Panel data show Gen Z shoppers return athletic apparel at roughly 1.5 times the rate of shoppers over 35.
evidence.note: Higher return rates among Gen Z raise the cost of a free exchange guarantee.

evidence.quote: Pace & Co. offers free returns within 60 days and says 70% of its range is priced under $50.
evidence.note: Free returns may already be expected rather than a differentiator.

metrics.label: Fit is the top frustration, Gen Z

gaps: No estimate of exchange cost or margin impact.

Panel figures from the analyst call are estimates, and the call notes are a thin source.

opportunities.title: Personalization as a premium tier
opportunities.status_rationale: Stated interest is real, but what customers did in the pilot did not confirm it.
opportunities.thesis: Personalization draws stated interest, but pilot behavior did not confirm it. Lead time looks like the binding constraint, not price alone.

evidence.quote: 38% of Gen Z respondents said they would pay a 15% premium for footwear personalized to their fit.
Custom colorway emails drove a 2.3x click through rate versus standard creative.
Personalized items in the pilot were returned at 11%, versus 16% for comparable standard items.
Customers who order a second pair within twelve months make up 31% of the Kinetic Lab customer base.
value_usd_bn: 1.1; yoy_growth_pct: 22.2; basis: Estimate
I would happily pay a bit more for shoes made to my foot, maybe 15% more, but only if they arrive as fast as normal ones.
evidence.note: A single respondent; a hypothesis only.

evidence.quote: When offered a 15% premium tier for personalized fit, only 9% of pilot shoppers selected it; most chose the free monogram option.
Across the 90 day observation window, pilot customers who bought a personalized product repurchased at 18%, compared with 24% for the matched control group.
Average lead time for personalized pairs was 12 days, and 41% of pilot exit survey respondents named the wait as their main reason not to order again.
Personalized orders were 2.4 times more likely than standard orders to generate a where is my order ticket.
The analyst expects personalization to remain below 5% of US athletic footwear units through 2028.
Personalization should stay a limited test in FY27 rather than a national launch until repeat purchase beats the control group.
evidence.note: Leadership direction: keep personalization a limited test.

evidence.quote: Leadership agreed to pause any national rollout of personalization until the full pilot readout in October.

opportunities.title: Social commerce and creator-led discovery
opportunities.status_rationale: Growth is clear; the economics are unproven.
opportunities.thesis: Social Shop is growing fastest and creator and peer discovery matter to Gen Z, but the channel is still small and shows lower order values and higher returns than stores.

evidence.quote: Social Shop sales grew 142% quarter over quarter, the fastest of any channel.
Social commerce platforms now account for 26% of Gen Z athletic footwear purchases, according to our 2026 panel.
Marketplace and social commerce together took 34% of Gen Z athletic spend in 2026, compared with 22% for brand owned sites.
I found my last three pairs through my run club group chat, not from ads.
We propose a FY27 Gen Z marketing budget of $24 million, of which 40% would shift to creator and community programs.
Median first response time on social channels slipped to 9.5 hours in Q3 against a service target of 4 hours.
evidence.note: Service on social channels lags the target.

opportunities.title: Materials and sustainability transparency
opportunities.status_rationale: Qualitative demand for proof is clear, but it is rarely the top frustration and the influence of sustainability claims is falling.
opportunities.thesis: Specific materials and origin information may build trust with Gen Z shoppers who discount generic green claims, but the commercial effect is untested.

evidence.quote: If a brand cannot tell me where the shoe was made and what is recycled in it, I just assume the green claims are marketing.
Put the recycled content percentage and the factory country right on the product page.
Participants ranked fit guarantee, faster delivery and honest materials information ahead of personalization when asked to spend a hypothetical 100 points.
The share of Gen Z respondents who say sustainability claims sway their brand choice has fallen to 54%.

metrics.label: Gen Z respondents naming sustainability transparency as top frustration

gaps: No data on conversion or willingness to pay for transparency.
caveats: Interview and survey verbatims are single people (n=1).
